description: AlphaZero-style self-play trains a network on games the search plays against itself, and the search provides what it learns from. Before each search, *Dirichlet noise* is mixed into the root's move priors, `(1 − fraction) · prior + fraction · η` with `η ~ Dirichlet(alpha)`, so even moves the network rules out get tried; `alpha = 0.3` and `fraction = 0.25` are AlphaZero's settings for chess. After the search, the visit distribution π over the root moves and the root value are the training target, with the game's final outcome added once it is over. The move to play is drawn from π by a *temperature*: at 0 the most visited move, at 1 in proportion to the visits, so early moves vary between games. Use it with PUCT and a policy-and-value network as the evaluator; the network, training loop and replay buffer stay outside the crate.
